bucket: circle entries describe stronger, more concrete advanced-academic and college-preparation pathways and supports (AP/IB, dual‑enrollment, early‑college, external partnerships, conservatory tracks) than square entries
definition: Multiple circle reviews enumerate programmatic college-prep offerings and outcomes—'AP and Honors classes,' 'IB program,' 'dual enrollment,' 'early college... over forty college credits,' and conservatory-style arts/music tracks—while square reviews emphasize limited AP breadth, low AP pass rates, or a lack of college-prep programming.

bucket: circle entries describe richer, more active community & extracurricular ecosystems (parent/PTA/booster involvement, alumni networks, business/nonprofit mentoring, robust arts/athletics) than square entries
definition: Circle reviews more often point to organized outside partnerships, strong PTAs/boosters, engaged alumni and named extracurricular strengths (marching band, art department, parent‑run fundraising, business mentoring programs), whereas square reviews rarely document comparable sustained community partnerships (examples: 'Social Venture Partners‑AZ mentoring,' 'The PTSA and the booster club really care,' 'state‑winning teams and active alumni').

bucket: circle entries report more administrative and staff dysfunctional practices (unresponsiveness, nepotism/favoritism, hiring problems, inconsistent teacher quality, counseling/special‑education failures, allegations of misconduct and discriminatory discipline) than square entries
definition: Many circle reviews accuse leadership of ignoring parents, protecting staff, hiring ex‑students, showing favoritism, failing special‑education and mental‑health needs, and even facing federal lawsuits or staff misconduct allegations, whereas square reviews are comparatively more likely to praise accessible leadership and consistent teacher support or to limit criticism to specific, isolated issues.

bucket: circle entries report stronger formal college‑preparatory programs, measurable academic outcomes, and advanced‑course/dual‑enrollment opportunities than square entries
definition: These reviews describe concrete programmatic offerings and outcomes tied to postsecondary readiness — e.g., Circle cites 8 AP courses, integrated ACT prep, dual‑enrollment/college‑credit partnerships (over 60 free college hours), measurable ACT and proficiency statistics, and high direct‑to‑college rates — while Square rarely provides quantified outcomes or institutional college‑credit pathways.

bucket: circle entries report more pervasive student-safety problems, bullying, fights, racial harassment, sexual harassment, gang activity, and administrative minimization or nonresponse than square entries
definition: This bucket captures reviewer reports of repeated physical fights, sexual harassment, racial taunts/ostracism, gang/drug activity and victims being ignored or even punished by staff (e.g., 'the bullying at this school is out of control', 'girls getting groped in packed hallways', 'students were told to go kill themselves', 'administrators said it is not bullying unless they physically hit you'). Square entries generally lack these widespread safety allegations and rarely describe staff tolerance of or inaction on severe peer abuse.
